subject: literature
passage: Miss Pryce had been told, in the agency's letter, that Thornleigh was a cheerful house, and she had resolved to find it so. When the housekeeper showed her to a room at the very top of the stairs, she remarked upon the fine prospect of the moor; when supper was brought up on a tray rather than served below, she said that she preferred a quiet meal after so long a journey; and when the lamp was found to hold barely an inch of oil, she observed that she had always been an early sleeper. Only after the housekeeper's step had died away did she sit down upon the narrow bed and allow herself, for the space of a minute, to look at the room as it was.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To portray a character who meets small slights with resolute cheer she drops only in private
choices.B: To suggest that Miss Pryce has been deceived by the agency and secretly plans to leave the house
choices.C: To describe the house at Thornleigh and the moorland landscape that surrounds it
choices.D: To show that the housekeeper deliberately mistreats Miss Pryce out of personal dislike

explanation.why: Miss Pryce "resolved to find" the house cheerful, and each disappointment (a top-floor room, supper on a tray, almost no lamp oil) gets a polite, positive remark. Only when alone does she let herself "look at the room as it was." The passage portrays her determined good cheer and the brief private moment when she sets it aside.
explanation.A: Correct. The series of cheerful replies to poor treatment, followed by her private, honest look at the room, is the passage's focus.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The letter's description may be optimistic, but nothing suggests Miss Pryce plans to leave; she allows herself only "a minute" of honesty.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The room and the moor are mentioned only as part of Miss Pryce's responses; the passage centers on her character.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text gives no motive for how Miss Pryce is treated; the housekeeper's feelings are never described.
